display.title: Episode 413: The Storyteller, Chapter 8
display.summary_short: A mailbox letter about loving Israel and Hashem our Father, chapter 8 of The Storyteller with a surprising secret revealed, Shema with a guest, and a class singing Chumash.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Rosh Chodesh Shevat 5750. The show opens with Uncle Yossi's mailbox: a young listener colored a flag reading 'I love Israel' and wrote 'I love Hashem, He is my Father.' Uncle Yossi explains that we love both the Jewish people and Eretz Yisroel, that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed because of baseless hatred, and that Ahavas Yisroel will bring Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, chapter 8 of The Storyteller: the Baal Shem Tov tells the feared official Alex that he is really a Jew named Yitzchak, saved as a child from a fire that took his parents and raised in an orphanage. Alex weeps, and the Baal Shem Tov tells him his soul has been calling him home. A girl whose letter was read on an earlier show comes to Studio 604 to say the Shema. The story continues as Yitzchak promises to move to a new town and learn Torah, and asks the Baal Shem Tov for a sign that his teshuvah has been accepted. After tzedakah, the guest's classmates sing a pasuk of Chumash with their classroom tune, followed by news of the Tzivos Hashem Children's Expo, candle time and the sponsor.
display.lesson: It is never too late to return to Hashem; every Jew's soul keeps calling him home.

date.note: 'This coming Friday is Erev Rosh Chodesh Shevat; this Shabbos is Rosh Chodesh Shevat' (1 Shevat 5750 = Shabbos 1990-01-27); candle lighting 4:47; Expo announced for February 7-13.
